title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete samples without first imputing values in the original feature space. It proposes the proximity kernel: equal-frequency bin centers per feature, proximity (Voronoi) assignment of observed values to bins, one-hot encoding into a sparse d×nbins representation, and a three-level cascading fallback (intersection → union → global prior) that fills missing encodings by kernel mean embedding. On 12 UCI incomplete datasets with K-means clustering measured by NMI, the proximity kernel reports the best average NMI (0.4245) against 9 imputation-based baselines while running in linear time.

match_target.why: Hepatitis is the smallest dataset in Table 3 (155 samples x 19 dims, 2 classes), so the full proximity-kernel pipeline (equal-frequency binning, proximity assignment, one-hot encoding, three-level cascading fallback, K-means with k=2, NMI) can be reproduced on a CPU in under a minute per run, while still exercising every component of the method and producing a directly comparable Table 3 number (0.2289).

tolerance.why: Rule 3: NMI is a bounded score printed in [0,1] and Hepatitis has only 155 samples (< 2000), and the paper gives no std for this value (only violin/box plots over 10 runs), so the band is 2.0 points on the 0-100 scale, i.e. 0.02 on the [0,1] scale the paper prints.

requirements.stmt: Bin centers for each feature must be selected by equal-frequency (percentile) binning of the observed values of that feature only, so that each bin holds approximately the same number of observed points.
requirements.quote: where each interval contains approximately the same number of data points.

requirements.stmt: Each observed value must be assigned to its nearest bin center (Voronoi/proximity assignment), not to the interval it falls in.
requirements.quote: we assign each observed value to its nearest center

requirements.stmt: Each feature's bin assignment must be expanded into a one-hot vector of length nbins and the per-sample encoding z_i is the concatenation across all d features (dimension d*nbins).
requirements.quote: After bin assignment, we encode each feature using one-hot representation.

requirements.stmt: Level-1 missing handling: match samples that fall in the same bin for ALL observed features of sample i (excluding i itself) and set the missing-feature encoding to the mean of their one-hot/bin encodings (kernel mean embedding).
requirements.quote: First, we seek samples matching across all observed features (intersection-based matching) and use their KME to represent the distribution of missing features.

requirements.stmt: Level-2 fallback: if the intersection set is empty, use the union of samples sharing at least one observed-feature bin with sample i and average their encodings for the missing features.
requirements.quote: If unsuccessful, we relax to samples matching on any observed feature (union-based matching).

requirements.stmt: Level-3 fallback: if the union set is also empty, set the missing feature's encoding to the global bin-frequency distribution p_{j,k} computed over samples where feature j is observed.
requirements.quote: Finally, we fall back to global distribution priors.

requirements.stmt: The similarity is K(x_m,x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n, i.e. the inner product of the encodings normalized by the number of features, giving a value in [0,1].
requirements.quote: The normalization by d yields the average co-occurrence rate across all features.

requirements.stmt: Clustering must be K-means with the number of clusters set to the ground-truth number of classes for every dataset.
requirements.quote: we applied K-means with the number of clusters to the ground-truth number of classes

requirements.stmt: Quality is measured by Normalized Mutual Information between the K-means partition and the ground-truth labels, averaged over 10 repeated runs per dataset.
requirements.quote: we evaluate all methods on clustering quality using Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) as the metric

requirements.stmt: Each configuration must be run 10 times and the average reported, matching the paper's stability protocol.
requirements.quote: Each experiment was conducted 10 times and report average results for stability.

requirements.stmt: The single hyperparameter nbins must be selected by searching {2,3,4,6,8} per dataset.
requirements.quote: For the proximity kernel, we search the number of bins per dimension in {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.

requirements.stmt: Bin centers must be estimated only from observed entries of each feature (missing entries never contribute to center selection or to global priors).
Encodings must be fractional (probabilistic over bins) for missing features, so the same inner-product kernel handles complete and incomplete samples uniformly.
requirements.quote: it computes the expected probability that two samples fall into the same bin, averaged across all features

data.name: UCI Machine Learning Repository (all 12 datasets: Kidney, Mammo, Heart, Hepatitis, Horse, Cancer/Wisconsin, Credit, Adult, Voting, Mushroom, Tumor, Soybean)
data.how_to_get: Download from the UCI archive https://archive.ics.uci.edu/datasets (paper footnote 1); read each file with '?' treated as NaN, class column held out as the NMI ground truth.
